title: Suspected acute compartment syndrome
logic: Limb injury or tight cast AND (pain out of proportion to injury OR pain on passive stretch of compartment muscles OR progressive paraesthesia OR tense swollen compartment) — pulses may still be present
action: Raise critical alert; split all circumferential casts/dressings to skin immediately; keep limb at heart level; senior surgical review now with emergency fasciotomy as the default outcome; do not delay for pressure measurement or imaging

title: Pulseless limb after fracture or dislocation
logic: Absent distal pulse or capillary refill over 3 seconds distal to a fracture/dislocation, before or after reduction
action: Emergency pathway: reduce/realign and reassess immediately; if perfusion not restored, escalate for surgical exploration or vascular referral within the ischaemia window; document times of injury, reduction and reassessment

title: Gustilo-Anderson grading required for open fractures
logic: Any fracture recorded with an overlying wound or marked 'open' AND no Gustilo-Anderson grade captured after the first debridement
action: Prompt the operating surgeon to assign Gustilo-Anderson grade (I, II, IIIA, IIIB, IIIC) intra-operatively — grading in casualty is provisional only; grade IIIB/IIIC triggers referral-level soft-tissue/vascular pathway

title: Open fracture bundle completeness
logic: Open fracture recorded AND any of: tetanus prophylaxis status missing, first IV antibiotic time missing, injury time missing
action: Block completion of the open-fracture record until tetanus status, antibiotic administration time and injury time are documented; flag antibiotic delay beyond 1 hour from arrival

title: Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis for implant surgery
logic: Booked procedure involves an implant (nail, plate, arthroplasty, wires) AND no prophylactic antibiotic recorded within 60 minutes before incision
action: Prompt anaesthetic/surgical team to give a first-generation cephalosporin (or per local policy where allergy documented) at induction, within 60 minutes before incision; record agent and time on the operative record

title: VTE prophylaxis after hip fracture surgery
logic: Patient over 40 with hip fracture or arthroplasty AND no VTE prophylaxis (pharmacological or mechanical) recorded within 24 hours post-operatively AND no contraindication documented
action: Prompt prescriber to start low-molecular-weight heparin per local protocol or, where unavailable/contraindicated, document mechanical prophylaxis and early mobilisation as the plan

title: Neurovascular observations after limb surgery or casting
logic: Limb surgery, manipulation or new circumferential cast completed within the last 24 hours
action: Schedule neurovascular observations (pain score, passive stretch pain, colour, warmth, capillary refill, sensation, movement, distal pulses) hourly for 4 hours then 4-hourly for 24 hours; any deterioration routes to the compartment-syndrome danger sign

title: Fracture clinic radiographic review
logic: Operatively or conservatively managed long-bone fracture discharged without a booked fracture-clinic appointment
action: Auto-propose follow-up: wound/cast check at 2 weeks, radiograph at 6 weeks, and union assessment at 3 months; paediatric supracondylar wires booked for removal at 3-4 weeks; flag non-attendance for community follow-up

title: Clubfoot brace compliance surveillance
logic: Ponseti tenotomy recorded AND child under 5 years AND no foot-abduction-brace review in the past 3 months
action: Generate community/clinic recall — bracing lapses are the leading cause of relapse; record brace condition and hours of wear at each visit
